mostWorthwhile.text: Supplying oxygen to the mitochondrion and then using its ATP for the pump made the connection from electron transfer and a hydrogen-ion gradient to cellular work concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the pump was the least engaging passage on its own: it was a straightforward placement, although separating installation from transport made sense.

surprise.text: The protein-making picture explicitly kept pyruvate out of the protein chain and showed ATP supporting amino acid preparation rather than becoming the protein.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the compatible menu made the choices easy; selecting mitochondrial rather than cytosolic ATP was a preference, not a discovered requirement.

continue.text: I would try another chapter: connecting respiration to membrane transport and protein-making was satisfying, and I would be curious to see how those connections extend to tissues.
